# SPLADE

**SPLADE** (Sparse Lexical and Expansion Model; Formal et al. 2021) is a retrieval algorithm that uses **sparse embeddings** — embeddings generated by BERT, then regularized to push most values to 0. It occupies an unusual position in the retrieval taxonomy: sparse by *representation* but dense by *behavior*.

## Why it matters to Huyen's taxonomy

[[ChipHuyen|Huyen]] uses SPLADE in [[ai-engineering-ch06-rag-agents|*AI Engineering* Ch 6]] as the load-bearing counterexample for **rejecting the literature's sparse-vs-dense division** of retrieval algorithms in favor of **term-based vs embedding-based**. SPLADE is the failure case for sparse-vs-dense:

> *"The sparse versus dense division causes SPLADE to be grouped together with term-based algorithms, even though SPLADE's operations, strengths, and weaknesses are much more similar to those of dense embedding retrieval than those of term-based retrieval."*

Under term-vs-embedding, SPLADE is correctly classified as [[EmbeddingBasedRetrieval|embedding-based]] — it just happens to use sparse embeddings instead of dense ones.

## Why sparsity helps

Sparse embedding operations are **more efficient** than dense embedding operations — most multiplications are by zero and can be skipped. SPLADE exploits this for indexing and query efficiency without giving up the semantic-match strengths of BERT-derived embeddings.

## Connections

- [[EmbeddingBasedRetrieval]] — the family SPLADE belongs to under Huyen's division.
- [[TermBasedRetrieval]] — the family SPLADE would be grouped with under the misclassifying sparse-vs-dense division.
- [[bert|BERT]] — the embedding backbone SPLADE regularizes.
- [[Embedding]] — the substrate.
- [[rag]] — the application surface.
- [[ai-engineering-ch06-rag-agents]] — primary source.
